keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

keywords.name: Vision-language models
keywords.about: Vision-language models are adapted for spatial reasoning, control, and multimodal benchmarks.

keywords.name: World models
keywords.about: Latent world models predict future states for planning, memory, and behavior.

keywords.name: Few-step diffusion
keywords.about: Caching and step distillation shrink image and action diffusion to few steps.

keywords.name: World-action models
keywords.about: World-action models jointly generate future observations and robot actions.

keywords.name: Hallucination mitigation
keywords.about: Contrastive and evidence-guided decoding reduces hallucinations in multimodal models.

keywords.name: Decision calibration
keywords.about: Calibrated rewards and Bayesian decision rules improve language-model decisions.

keywords.name: Retrieval and memory
keywords.about: Agents combine retrieval, knowledge graphs, and lossless memory for long-horizon question answering.

keywords.name: Flow matching
keywords.about: Flow-matching objectives train robot policies, world-action models, and image generators.

keywords.name: Abstention
keywords.about: Models learn to abstain or defer when uncertainty or risk is high.

keywords.name: JEPA
keywords.about: Joint-embedding predictive architectures are diagnosed and adapted for planning and video.

keywords.name: Robot replanning
keywords.about: Robots diagnose stalls and replan tasks under changing constraints.

keywords.name: Biomedical ML
keywords.about: Biomedical models handle missing covariates, censored events, and phenotype uncertainty.

keywords.name: Manipulation benchmarks
keywords.about: Simulated manipulation benchmarks and audits expose false successes in robot policies.

keywords.name: Agent compliance
keywords.about: LLM agents are audited and monitored for legal, policy, and misconduct compliance.

themes.name: World-action models and vision-language-action policy learning
themes.summary: Papers develop world-action models and vision-language-action policies that predict future scene evolution and robot actions for manipulation, navigation, and loco-manipulation. They differ by emphasizing multi-agent coordination, long-horizon planning, verification, memory, residual learning, tactile refinement, and accelerated inference.

themes.name: 3D reconstruction, spatial grounding, and scene understanding
themes.summary: Papers reconstruct three-dimensional objects and scenes and ground spatial relationships using implicit representations, Gaussian splatting, mesh optimization, depth completion, and multimodal scene graphs. They range from single-video mesh reconstruction and relighting to egocentric passage benchmarks and visual grounding.

themes.name: Adversarial attacks, defenses, and watermarking for foundation models
themes.summary: Papers study adversarial threats and defenses for foundation models, including sparse attacks, cross-modal semantic attacks, watermark forgery resistance, fingerprinting, and detection of manipulated robot policies. They differ by targeting images, multi-agent language systems, visible-infrared models, and world-action policies through texture or universal perturbations.

themes.name: Diffusion-model acceleration and controllable generation
themes.summary: Papers accelerate diffusion and flow models through caching, distillation, and test-time search while improving controllability for text rendering, panorama generation, sequential editing, and long video. They differ by calibrating cached features, preserving latent reconstruction, and using rewards or previews to guide generation.

themes.name: KV-cache and visual-token compression for efficient inference
themes.summary: Papers reduce inference memory by compressing key-value caches and visual tokens for long-context, video, document, and world-action models. They differ through eviction, quantization, pruning, and budget-aware token selection, including query-aware versus query-agnostic video pruning.

themes.name: Agent safety, compliance, and trustworthy execution
themes.summary: Papers examine safety and compliance of autonomous agents, covering legal hiring evaluations, computer-use and mobile execution controls, browser-model abuse, cyber-physical hallucinations, and unfaithful work reports. They differ by proposing monitoring engines, intervention layers, stress-testing testbeds, and impossibility arguments for agent safety verification.

themes.name: Sparse autoencoders and representation-level interpretability
themes.summary: Papers use sparse autoencoders, attribution, and routing analyses to interpret internal model representations and reasoning. They differ by separating reconstruction from interpretability, auditing weather and vision-language models, and testing whether routing states causally support step-level verification.

themes.name: Long-horizon agents with memory and context compaction
themes.summary: Papers address long-horizon agents that must retain, retrieve, revise, and compact memory across extended tasks. They differ by using lossless index-free memory, parametric memory decay, temporal persona dossiers, memory-drift detection, and selective answer revision.

themes.name: Medical multimodal reasoning and clinical safety auditing
themes.summary: Papers build medical multimodal models and auditing tools for clinical safety, including harm juries, verbalized-thought monitoring, anomaly detection, three-dimensional foundation features, mammography evidence selection, multilingual reasoning, and registration adaptation. They differ by evaluating response harms, probing internal states, and improving lesion-aware or language-balanced reasoning.

themes.name: Autonomous scientific discovery and self-driving laboratories
themes.summary: Papers develop AI agents for autonomous scientific research, experiment planning, and self-driving laboratories with authorization, auditing, and multiverse analysis. They differ by closing analyze-to-design gaps, probing problem structure, and testing the robustness of empirical finance conclusions across analytical choices.

themes.name: LLM-judge reliability and benchmark auditing
themes.summary: Papers audit LLM judges and benchmark evaluators for calibration, rubric sensitivity, success-checker failures, and transfer of judge knowledge. They differ by training calibrated decision rewards, exposing scale-direction bias, ranking rubric coverage, and diagnosing physics benchmark scoring artifacts.

themes.name: Language agents for hardware design, RTL, and EDA
themes.summary: Papers apply language-model agents to hardware design verification, RTL generation and repair, EDA reinforcement learning, and embedded board-level design. They differ by building benchmarks, verification-gated workflows, target-aware HLS generation, dependency views for repair, and holistic device agents.

highlights.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
highlights.theme: Agent safety, compliance, and trustworthy execution
highlights.why: It formally proves agent safety undecidable when a language model is coupled with a general computing device, a foundational negative result.
highlights.key_result: We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable. Specifically, the problem is PSPACE-complete even when the description of the agent is known.
evidence: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable.

Under finite constraints (bounded context, values and running time) safety is decidable but still intractable. Specifically, the problem is PSPACE-complete even when the description of the agent is known.

highlights.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
highlights.authors: Zirui Song, Jiadong Zhang, Zheng Lu et al.
highlights.why: It audits success checkers in simulated manipulation benchmarks, revealing widespread phantom successes and silent failures that undermine benchmark validity.
highlights.key_result: SimAudit identified 61 distinct checker defects across 49 tasks in RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures. After repairing the defects, the original and repaired checkers disagree on up to 9.1% of a policy's rollouts.
evidence: We identify 61 defects across 49 tasks in RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures.
After repairing the defects, we score the same rollouts from released policies with both checkers. The original and repaired checkers disagree on up to 9.1% of a policy's rollouts.

highlights.title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
highlights.theme: Autonomous scientific discovery and self-driving laboratories
highlights.why: It uses AI agents to run a multiverse analysis across 324 finance papers, quantifying how much published claims depend on analytical choices.
highlights.key_result: In this paper, we use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments and combine the results in a meta-analysis; across the 304 directional claims we compare, the mean share supported is 25%, and we reproduce 42% of the main estimates of directional claims with a published test.
evidence: In this paper, we use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments and combine the results in a meta-analysis. Across the 304 directional claims we compare, the mean share supported, i.e., the share of specifications that keep the directional claim, is 25%. This share is zero for 23% of the claims, and the median claim has a median signed z of 0.70. We reproduce 42% of the main estimates of directional claims with a published test.

highlights.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
highlights.why: Across extensive RL runs, it shows judge blind spots transfer to models while judge knowledge does not, a counterintuitive result for judge-based training.
highlights.key_result: A model trained by reinforcement learning takes two things from its grader to new questions: how often to answer, and which kinds of question to give up. It leaves behind the grader's knowledge of which answers are right: that knowledge corrects only about one answer in a hundred.
evidence: A model trained by reinforcement learning takes two things from its grader to new questions: how often to answer, and which kinds of question to give up. It leaves behind the grader's knowledge of which answers are right: that knowledge corrects only about one answer in a hundred.

highlights.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models
highlights.authors: Yihan Wang, Haochen Sun, Xi He et al.
highlights.theme: Adversarial attacks, defenses, and watermarking for foundation models
highlights.why: It proposes Tripwire-WM, the first forgery-evident undetectable watermarking framework, addressing a key limitation of existing provenance schemes.
highlights.key_result: The paper proposes Tripwire-WM, the first forgery-evident framework for undetectable watermarks, which rejects and reports forgeries. On MS-COCO, it accepts no imprinting forgery (up to 55.0% for SemBind) and at most 1.8% of reprompting forgeries (up to 46.2% for SemBind), while accepting at least 99% of genuine watermarked images at 10^{-6} FPR and matching the robustness of the base schemes.
evidence: We propose Tripwire-WM, the first forgery-evident framework for undetectable watermarks. It commits the semantics of the generated image to the magnitudes of the initial latent noise, which the sign-based watermarks leave unused, through a distribution-preserving embedding; a forged image carries a valid watermark but with a commitment that does not match its content, so the detector both rejects it and reports it as forged.

On MS-COCO, with the owner's own model as the surrogate, it accepts no imprinting forgery, compared with up to 55.0% for SemBind, and reports all of them as forged; it also accepts at most 1.8% of reprompting forgeries, against up to 46.2% for SemBind.
Meanwhile, it accepts at least 99% of genuine watermarked images at 10^{-6} FPR and matches the robustness of the base schemes.

highlights.title: VoxForge: A Unified Foundation Model for Dense 3D Features Across MRI, CT and PET
highlights.theme: Medical multimodal reasoning and clinical safety auditing
highlights.why: It presents VoxForge, a unified foundation model for dense 3D features across MRI, CT, and PET that performs competitively while frozen.
highlights.key_result: VoxForge has the best or tied-best average rank in every task group, serves localized and global tasks across modalities at the level of state-of-the-art specialists, and is extremely label-efficient, matching top-performing models on TotalSegmentator CT with a tenth of the labels.
evidence: VoxForge has the best or tied-best average rank in every task group, serves localized and global tasks across modalities at the level of state-of-the-art specialists, and is extremely label-efficient, matching top-performing models on TotalSegmentator CT with a tenth of the labels.

highlights.title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
highlights.authors: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo et al.
highlights.theme: World-action models and vision-language-action policy learning
highlights.why: It provides a clear diagnostic separating search failures from scoring failures in visual world-model planners, guiding better remedies.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that world-model planners fail either because CEM misses solutions that its cost prefers or because it picks actions that the model overrates; a few tasks with known solutions tell which, and so which remedies can help. Acting on the regime pays off: where the model misjudges, averaging without it solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 for its choice among the same windows, and within PushT our rule solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.
evidence: World-model planners fail either because CEM misses solutions that its cost prefers or because it picks actions that the model overrates. A few tasks with known solutions tell which, and so which remedies can help: more search and more candidates in the first case, plans that stay with the demonstrations or a better model in the second. With retrieved demonstrations, the better use follows the regime across our environments and, within PushT, flips once scoring failures are frequent. Acting on the regime pays off: where the model misjudges, averaging without it solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 for its choice among the same windows, and within PushT our rule solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

highlights.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
highlights.authors: Xuwei Ding, Skylar Zhai, Linxin Song et al.
highlights.theme: 3D reconstruction, spatial grounding, and scene understanding
highlights.why: It introduces TuringSpace, interactive CAPTCHAs that test spatial grounding through action, revealing a significant gap between humans and multimodal models.
highlights.key_result: On TuringSpace-Bench , frontier MLLMs fall well short of humans, reaching at best 74.1% against 94.1%. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B in TuringSpace-Gym raises its success rate from 1.6% to 33.1% and improves it on all seven OOD benchmarks.

news.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
news.summary: Google Quantum AI reported in a Science paper that it demonstrated measurement contextuality on its superconducting Willow processor, winning the magic square game 98.3% of the time and beating classical strategies on tasks spanning up to 105 qubits. The authors argue these contextuality tasks serve as a benchmark that catches subtle hardware errors that random-circuit tests miss.

news.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
news.summary: Google launched Tool Retrieval in preview in the Gemini Interactions API, letting agents load tool parameter schemas on demand by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading to true, rather than sending the full tool library in each prompt. It works with Gemini 3.6 and later, runs search server-side with no index to host, supports prefix caching and remote MCP servers, and offers a client-side mode with "execution": "client" that adds one round trip per search.

news.title: Walter Isaacson on curiosity and creativity in the AI age.
news.summary: Google's Dialogues on Technology and Society podcast released an episode in which Kent Walker speaks with biographer and historian Walter Isaacson about curiosity and human judgment in the AI era, framed around da Vinci, Franklin and Lovelace. No technical specifics are given beyond the episode's availability.

news.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
news.summary: NVIDIA and Microsoft announced at Ignite expanded Azure access to NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, availability of NVIDIA open models and customization via Microsoft Foundry, and edge AI options, with Microsoft using NVIDIA Dynamo and RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing models. Cited results include Azure scaling to 10,240 NVIDIA GPUs with GB200 NVL72 on DeepSeek-V3 in MLPerf Training v6.1, a lead of over 10% on DeepSeek-R1 interactive throughput for GB300 NVL72 in MLPerf Inference v6.1, and EY reporting a 55% accuracy gain and 15x lower cost using Programmed Training with Nemotron models.

news.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA described developer projects combining frontier models with Omniverse libraries, including Falkor's Surface platform using GPT-6 Astra and RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Azure to build facility-scale digital twins, and an Isaac Sim pick-and-place simulation assembled by an agent using GPT-6 Sol. A community developer directed GPT-6 Astra and Claude Code (about eight hours of agent work over a weekend) to build a voice-controlled VR application on an RTX 6000 Ada workstation and Meta Quest 3.

news.title: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW
news.summary: GeForce NOW announced Black Friday promotions: 30% off the first six months of new Performance or Ultimate memberships through Nov. 30, and 90% off the first month via Amazon through Dec. 31 on supported Fire TV devices. The service expands to Fire TV Stick HD, 4K Select and 4K (2026 model) on Vega OS, adds streaming up to 5K or 360 fps with DLSS 5, and adds nine games this week including five Bethesda titles with GOG support.

news.title: Reducing Rollout Bottlenecks in Reinforcement Learning with NVIDIA Dynamo
news.summary: NVIDIA described how Dynamo serves as a rollout layer for reinforcement learning training, using KV-aware routing to balance cache reuse against worker load, ModelExpress to distribute compressed delta weight updates, and recovery mechanisms that reroute requests and let replacement workers catch up from checkpoints. It lists open-source integrations with verl, NeMo RL, Slime and prime-rl.

news.title: Enabling Real-Time AI for Scientific Instruments with GPU-Native Data Acquisition
news.summary: NVIDIA detailed DAQIRI, a Holoscan data acquisition library that receives detector packets directly into GPU memory, used with a high-dynamic-range electron microscopy camera at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory that produces over 500 Gbps, described as over 500x faster than conventional EELS data streams. The latest release adds hardware packet reordering on ConnectX-7 or newer NICs, an ibverbs engine that nearly doubles per-core throughput at small packet sizes, and a direct polling mode with 2-4 µs send-to-receive latency.

news.title: Build Tool-Calling Parsers in Rust with AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced frontend-crates, reusable Rust components that parse tool calls from LLM output into structured events, with documented recovery rules for malformed, incomplete and streaming inputs. A shared Conformance Corpus pairs model-specific inputs with expected GOLDEN outputs, enabling UNIFIED.* test cases to be reused across model families including Beam, GPT-OSS, Muse Spark and NVIDIA Nemotron 3, with an example using the dynamo-parsers-v2 crate.

news.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
news.summary: AWS added AWS Billing as a payment option in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments, letting agents buy x402-enabled AWS Marketplace products in USD billed to the developer's AWS account, without stablecoin wallets or API keys; AgentCore payments reached general availability in August 2026. Developers create a Payment Manager with an AWS Billing connector and per-task payment sessions with spending limits, purchases are auditable in CloudTrail and Cost Explorer, and a new AgentCore Gateway connector supports discovery, with the x402 exact scheme supported at launch.

news.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
news.summary: AWS described how the BMW Group governs agentic AI across R&D, where more than 12,500 developers work on approximately 500 million lines of code and a backend of over 1,300 microservices serving 24 million vehicles. The approach centers on an agent harness runtime, framework-agnostic governance externalized at an MCP gateway and agent registry, graduated autonomy levels (0 human-in-the-loop, 1 human-on-the-loop, 2 autonomous within guardrails), and five practices codified as infrastructure as code, drawn from work since 2023.

news.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
news.summary: Amazon announced the Selling Partner plugin for AWS Quick at Amazon Accelerate on September 23, 2026, launching in beta to connect AWS Quick to live Seller Central data for listings, inventory and sales. A limited-time offer gives every primary selling account holder 12 months of AWS Quick Plus free plus access for 10 additional users if they sign up by December 31, 2026, and AWS states seller data is not used to train models.

news.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI added monitoring that detects latency drift, idle GPUs and configuration gaps on generative AI inference endpoints, on by default for endpoints using vLLM serving containers and GPU instances with no setup required. It uses only operational signals (latency, GPU utilization, serving configuration) and not request or response content, sends one AWS Health notification per endpoint, and links to a SageMaker Studio agentic experience that benchmarks alternatives on separate compute before any change is applied.

highlights.title: Pandora's Toolbox Or Why Agent Safety Cannot Be Verified
highlights.theme: Agent safety, compliance, and trustworthy execution
highlights.why: 它形式化地证明了当语言模型与通用计算设备耦合时，智能体安全性不可判定，这是一个基础性的否定结果。
highlights.key_result: 我们表明这种耦合使得安全性不可判定。具体而言，即使智能体的描述已知，该问题也是PSPACE-complete的。
evidence: Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable.

Under finite constraints (bounded context, values and running time) safety is decidable but still intractable. Specifically, the problem is PSPACE-complete even when the description of the agent is known.

highlights.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
highlights.authors: Zirui Song, Jiadong Zhang, Zheng Lu et al.
highlights.why: 它审计了模拟操作基准中的成功检查器，揭示了普遍存在的幻影成功和静默失败，这些缺陷损害了基准的有效性。
highlights.key_result: SimAudit在RoboTwin 2.0、RoboCasa365和RoboDojo的49个任务中识别出61个不同的检查器缺陷，其中包括40个幻影成功和21个静默失败。修复这些缺陷后，原始检查器和修复后的检查器在策略的rollout中最多有9.1%的结果不一致。
evidence: We identify 61 defects across 49 tasks in RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures.
After repairing the defects, we score the same rollouts from released policies with both checkers. The original and repaired checkers disagree on up to 9.1% of a policy's rollouts.

highlights.title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
highlights.theme: Autonomous scientific discovery and self-driving laboratories
highlights.why: 它使用AI智能体对324篇金融学论文进行多宇宙分析，量化已发表声明在多大程度上依赖于分析选择。
highlights.key_result: 在本文中，我们使用AI智能体对324篇复用13个自然实验的论文进行多宇宙分析，并将结果合并到一个元分析中；在我们比较的304个方向性声明中，受支持的平均比例为25%，我们使用已发表的检验复现了方向性声明中42%的主要估计值。
evidence: In this paper, we use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments and combine the results in a meta-analysis. Across the 304 directional claims we compare, the mean share supported, i.e., the share of specifications that keep the directional claim, is 25%. This share is zero for 23% of the claims, and the median claim has a median signed z of 0.70. We reproduce 42% of the main estimates of directional claims with a published test.

highlights.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
highlights.why: 在大量RL运行中，它表明评判者的盲区会迁移到模型中，而评判者的知识不会，这对基于评判者的训练来说是一个反直觉的结果。
highlights.key_result: 通过强化学习训练的模型从其评分者那里带到新问题上的有两样东西：多久回答一次，以及放弃哪些类型的问题。它没有继承评分者关于哪些答案正确的知识：这种知识只纠正大约百分之一的答案。
evidence: A model trained by reinforcement learning takes two things from its grader to new questions: how often to answer, and which kinds of question to give up. It leaves behind the grader's knowledge of which answers are right: that knowledge corrects only about one answer in a hundred.

highlights.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models
highlights.authors: Yihan Wang, Haochen Sun, Xi He et al.
highlights.theme: Adversarial attacks, defenses, and watermarking for foundation models
highlights.why: 它提出了Tripwire-WM，这是第一个防伪可验证的不可检测水印框架，解决了现有来源方案的一个关键局限。
highlights.key_result: 本文提出了Tripwire-WM，这是第一个针对不可检测水印的防伪取证框架，能够拒绝并报告伪造。在MS-COCO上，它不接受任何压印伪造（SemBind最多为55.0%），最多接受1.8%的重新提示伪造（SemBind最多为46.2%），同时在10^{-6} FPR下接受至少99%的真实水印图像，并且鲁棒性与基础方案相当。
evidence: We propose Tripwire-WM, the first forgery-evident framework for undetectable watermarks. It commits the semantics of the generated image to the magnitudes of the initial latent noise, which the sign-based watermarks leave unused, through a distribution-preserving embedding; a forged image carries a valid watermark but with a commitment that does not match its content, so the detector both rejects it and reports it as forged.

On MS-COCO, with the owner's own model as the surrogate, it accepts no imprinting forgery, compared with up to 55.0% for SemBind, and reports all of them as forged; it also accepts at most 1.8% of reprompting forgeries, against up to 46.2% for SemBind.
Meanwhile, it accepts at least 99% of genuine watermarked images at 10^{-6} FPR and matches the robustness of the base schemes.

highlights.title: VoxForge: A Unified Foundation Model for Dense 3D Features Across MRI, CT and PET
highlights.theme: Medical multimodal reasoning and clinical safety auditing
highlights.why: 它提出了VoxForge，这是一个针对MRI、CT和PET的稠密3D特征的统一基础模型，在冻结状态下仍具有竞争力。
highlights.key_result: VoxForge在每个任务组中都具有最佳或并列最佳的平均排名，能够以最先进专家模型的水平服务于跨模态的局部和全局任务，并且极其标签高效，在TotalSegmentator CT上以十分之一的标签匹配了表现最佳的模型。
evidence: VoxForge has the best or tied-best average rank in every task group, serves localized and global tasks across modalities at the level of state-of-the-art specialists, and is extremely label-efficient, matching top-performing models on TotalSegmentator CT with a tenth of the labels.

highlights.title: Search or Scoring? Diagnosing Why Visual World-Model Planners Fail
highlights.authors: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Shang Luo et al.
highlights.theme: World-action models and vision-language-action policy learning
highlights.why: 它提供了一种清晰的诊断方法，将视觉世界模型规划器中的搜索失败与评分失败区分开来，为更好的补救措施提供指导。
highlights.key_result: 本文表明，世界模型规划器失败的原因要么是CEM错过了其代价偏好的解决方案，要么是它选择了模型高估的动作；少数已知解决方案的任务可以说明是哪种原因，从而知道哪些补救措施可以起作用。根据这种机制采取行动会带来回报：在模型误判的情况下，不使用模型进行平均可以解决168个新的Metaworld任务中的127个，而在相同窗口内其选择最多只能解决87个；在PushT中，我们的规则可以解决960个新回合中的678个，而最佳固定使用方式只能解决530个。
evidence: World-model planners fail either because CEM misses solutions that its cost prefers or because it picks actions that the model overrates. A few tasks with known solutions tell which, and so which remedies can help: more search and more candidates in the first case, plans that stay with the demonstrations or a better model in the second. With retrieved demonstrations, the better use follows the regime across our environments and, within PushT, flips once scoring failures are frequent. Acting on the regime pays off: where the model misjudges, averaging without it solves 127 of 168 new Metaworld tasks, against at most 87 for its choice among the same windows, and within PushT our rule solves 678 of 960 new episodes, against 530 for the best fixed use.

highlights.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
highlights.authors: Xuwei Ding, Skylar Zhai, Linxin Song et al.
highlights.theme: 3D reconstruction, spatial grounding, and scene understanding
highlights.why: 它引入了TuringSpace，这是一种通过动作测试空间接地的交互式CAPTCHA，揭示了人类与多模态模型之间的显著差距。
highlights.key_result: 在TuringSpace-Bench上，前沿MLLM远未达到人类水平，最高仅为74.1%，而人类为94.1%。在TuringSpace-Gym中对Qwen3.5-9B进行微调后，其成功率从1.6%提高到33.1%，并在全部七个OOD基准上都有所改善。
evidence: On TuringSpace-Bench , frontier MLLMs fall well short of humans, reaching at best 74.1% against 94.1%. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B in TuringSpace-Gym raises its success rate from 1.6% to 33.1% and improves it on all seven OOD benchmarks.

news.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
news.summary: Google Quantum AI在一篇Science论文中报告，它在超导Willow处理器上展示了测量语境性，在魔方游戏中获胜率为98.3%，并在覆盖多达105个量子比特的任务中击败了经典策略。作者认为，这些语境性任务可以作为一种基准，捕捉随机线路测试所遗漏的细微硬件错误。

news.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
news.summary: Google在Gemini Interactions API中预览发布了Tool Retrieval，允许智能体通过添加tool_search工具并将defer_loading设置为true来按需加载工具参数模式，而无需在每个提示中发送完整的工具库。它适用于Gemini 3.6及更高版本，在服务器端运行搜索而无需托管索引，支持前缀缓存和远程MCP服务器，并提供客户端模式，其中"execution": "client"每次搜索会增加一次往返。

news.title: Walter Isaacson on curiosity and creativity in the AI age.
news.summary: Google的Dialogues on Technology and Society播客发布了一集，Kent Walker与传记作家兼历史学家Walter Isaacson围绕达·芬奇、富兰克林和洛夫莱斯讨论了AI时代的好奇心和人类判断力。除该集已上线外，没有给出具体技术细节。

news.title: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs
news.summary: NVIDIA和Microsoft在Ignite大会上宣布扩大Azure对NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72系统的访问，通过Microsoft Foundry提供NVIDIA开放模型和定制，以及边缘AI选项，Microsoft使用NVIDIA Dynamo和RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU来服务Bing模型。引用的结果包括：Azure在MLPerf Training v6.1中使用GB200 NVL72在DeepSeek-V3上扩展到10,240个NVIDIA GPU；在MLPerf Inference v6.1中，GB300 NVL72在DeepSeek-R1交互吞吐量上领先超过10%；EY报告使用Programmed Training和Nemotron模型实现了55%的准确率提升和15x的成本降低。

news.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA described developer projects combining frontier models with Omniverse libraries, including Falkor's Surface platform using GPT-6 Astra and RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition GPUs on Azure to build facility-scale digital twins, and an Isaac Sim pick-and-place simulation assembled by an agent using GPT-6 Sol. A community developer directed GPT-6 Astra and Claude Code (about eight hours of agent work over a weekend) to build a voice-controlled VR application on an RTX 6000 Ada workstation and Meta Quest 3.

news.title: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW
news.summary: GeForce NOW announced Black Friday promotions: 30% off the first six months of new Performance or Ultimate memberships through Nov. 30, and 90% off the first month via Amazon through Dec. 31 on supported Fire TV devices. The service expands to Fire TV Stick HD, 4K Select and 4K (2026 model) on Vega OS, adds streaming up to 5K or 360 fps with DLSS 5, and adds nine games this week including five Bethesda titles with GOG support.

news.title: Reducing Rollout Bottlenecks in Reinforcement Learning with NVIDIA Dynamo
news.summary: NVIDIA描述了Dynamo如何作为强化学习训练的rollout层，使用KV感知路由在缓存重用与工作负载之间取得平衡，使用ModelExpress分发压缩的增量权重更新，并使用恢复机制重新路由请求，让替代工作节点从检查点追赶进度。文中列出了与verl、NeMo RL、Slime和prime-rl的开源集成。

news.title: Enabling Real-Time AI for Scientific Instruments with GPU-Native Data Acquisition
news.summary: NVIDIA详细介绍了DAQIRI，这是一个Holoscan数据采集库，可将探测器数据包直接接收到GPU内存中，与劳伦斯伯克利国家实验室的一台高动态范围电子显微镜相机配合使用，该相机产生超过500 Gbps的数据，据称比传统EELS数据流快500x以上。最新版本在ConnectX-7或更新的NIC上增加了硬件数据包重排序功能，增加了一个在小数据包大小时几乎将每核吞吐量翻倍的ibverbs引擎，并增加了一个发送到接收延迟为2-4 µs的直接轮询模式。

news.title: Build Tool-Calling Parsers in Rust with AI Agents
news.summary: NVIDIA推出了frontend-crates，这是可复用的Rust组件，可将LLM输出中的工具调用解析为结构化事件，并提供了针对格式错误、不完整和流式输入的文档化恢复规则。共享的Conformance Corpus将针对特定模型的输入与预期的GOLDEN输出配对，使UNIFIED.*测试用例能够在包括Beam、GPT-OSS、Muse Spark和NVIDIA Nemotron 3在内的模型系列中复用，并提供了一个使用dynamo-parsers-v2 crate的示例。

news.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
news.summary: AWS added AWS Billing as a payment option in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments, letting agents buy x402-enabled AWS Marketplace products in USD billed to the developer's AWS account, without stablecoin wallets or API keys; AgentCore payments reached general availability in August 2026. Developers create a Payment Manager with an AWS Billing connector and per-task payment sessions with spending limits, purchases are auditable in CloudTrail and Cost Explorer, and a new AgentCore Gateway connector supports discovery, with the x402 exact scheme supported at launch.

news.title: How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
news.summary: AWS描述了BMW集团如何在研发中治理代理式AI，超过12,500名开发人员在约500 million行代码以及一个包含超过1,300个微服务、服务24 million辆汽车的后端上工作。该方法的中心是一个智能体挂载运行时，将框架无关的治理外部化到MCP网关和智能体注册中心，采用分级自主级别（0 human-in-the-loop，1 human-on-the-loop，2 autonomous within guardrails），并将五项实践编纂为基础设施即代码，这些实践源自2023年以来的工作。

news.title: Run your whole selling business in AWS Quick
news.summary: Amazon announced the Selling Partner plugin for AWS Quick at Amazon Accelerate on September 23, 2026, launching in beta to connect AWS Quick to live Seller Central data for listings, inventory and sales. A limited-time offer gives every primary selling account holder 12 months of AWS Quick Plus free plus access for 10 additional users if they sign up by December 31, 2026, and AWS states seller data is not used to train models.

news.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI增加了监控功能，可检测生成式AI推理端点上的延迟漂移、空闲GPU和配置缺口；对于使用vLLM服务容器和GPU实例的端点默认启用，无需任何设置。它仅使用运行信号（延迟、GPU利用率、服务配置），不使用请求或响应内容，每个端点发送一条AWS Health通知，并链接到SageMaker Studio代理式体验，该体验在任何更改应用之前会在独立计算资源上对替代方案进行基准测试。
